summary.headline: S Chand Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs1,145m, but EBITDA loss of Rs97m and PAT loss of Rs187m widened the reported loss.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs1,145m, up 12% YoY, with gross margin improved. EBITDA turned to a loss of Rs97m and PAT to a loss of Rs187m, hit by marketing costs pulled into Q1 from Q2 and a one-time tax rate adjustment. Management pre-bought paper ahead of expected price rises, lifting inventory and slightly raising net working capital days. Net cash reached a record Rs1,182m after Rs141m dividend, and FY27 guidance of 10-15% operating revenue growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin was reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Wider loss YoY due to one-time tax rate adjustment
vs Rs1,160m in Q4FY26, after Rs141m dividend

segments.name: School Education (K-12)
segments.commentary: Refreshed curriculum brands Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK and Solid Steps received repeat adoptions; Mylestone (650+ schools) and My Zen (about 500 schools) together generated about Rs55-60 crore in FY26. New partnerships with Allied, Jump Maths, Penguin and Speedlabs added to the offering.

segments.name: Content Licensing
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue of about Rs9 crore (Rs91m); about Rs14 crore booked to date. Target is above Rs40 crore for FY27 and growing active clients from 5 to 10.

segments.name: International (CPD Singapore, acquired)
segments.commentary: Q1 contribution about Rs1 crore; target of SGD 1m (about Rs7.5 crore) by year end. Management says it was profitable earlier, currently investing in content and marketing with limited burn; India and Middle East K-12 expansion will take 1-2 academic cycles.

guidance_outlook: Operating revenue growth of 10-15% for FY27.
EBITDA margin guidance of 17-19% for FY27, stated to include a 10-12% paper price increase assumption.
Content licensing revenue target above Rs40 crore in FY27.
Market buyback under consideration; management expects a decision by October 2026, contingent on acquisitions progressing.
Acquisitions under discussion in test prep and school spaces, total size about Rs40-50 crore at most.
Steady-state growth for core business of 10-12% over the next 2-3 years, excluding acquisitions and new segments.
Full adoption of NCERT new-syllabus books expected in FY27; West Bengal new syllabus expected to support growth for about 2 years from next year.
capex_capacity: New printing and binding facility: half to be completed in FY27, full completion in FY28; partial binding and printing to start from the following week, with operations in September-October 2026.
Management says the facility covers requirements for 10-15 years and should improve productivity, quality and output speed.
demand_pricing: Dollar rate cited at about Rs95 versus about Rs85 a year earlier, raising imported paper cost along with logistics and Middle East tensions.
Paper availability is not a constraint; management says the issue is price. About 20-25% of annual paper requirement purchased so far, roughly 3-4 months earlier than usual.
Receivable days stable; collections from the Middle East are being hit by geopolitical instability and are expected to normalise.
Management is cautious on paper inventory due to space and cash limits, so it will not buy the full annual requirement.
Regional board growth (Chhaya Prakashani) was lumpy in FY26 due to West Bengal elections shifting sales into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company buy paper early and where are paper prices heading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pre-bought to hedge against higher USD-linked import costs, logistics and Middle East tensions; paper prices may firm up next quarter. About 25% of annual consumption bought, versus the usual August-October purchase window.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 17-19% margin guidance inclusive of paper price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Guidance assumes a 10-12% paper price increase; management said a 40% rise would be a different case.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of buyback and acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: A market buyback is being considered, with a decision targeted by October once acquisitions progress. Two acquisition discussions in test prep and school space, total size Rs40-50 crore at most.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state growth outlook beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Core business steady state is 10-12%, built from 3-4% student growth, 4-5% volume and 4-5% pricing; acquisitions or new segments would add to this.

qa_highlights.question: Will goodwill be revalued or impaired?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not impair now because the acquired investments have intrinsic value. Impairment may be considered in a year with exceptional income, such as a real estate sale or Smartivity listing.

risks_watch: Paper cost inflation versus the 10-12% assumed in the 17-19% margin guidance; further USD-INR weakness or freight disruption would pressure margins.
Working capital: higher inventory from early paper purchases and Middle East collection delays; cash deployment on paper versus buyback.
Q1 EBITDA loss partly reflects marketing timing (Q2 costs in Q1), so the Q2 margin needs watching.
Content licensing must scale from about Rs14 crore to above Rs40 crore; contracts not yet signed.
Large goodwill on the balance sheet weighs on return ratios; no impairment or revaluation planned near term.
Buyback decision and acquisition progress, targeted for October 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core K-12 franchise and content licensing, but cautious on paper prices and working capital. Management was non-committal on the timing of the buyback and on content licensing contracts, and deflected goodwill questions.
key_quotes: We took a conscious decision to advance Paper purchases since we are pre -empting higher paper prices, supply disruptions and elongated shipping timelines for imported paper.
The steady state is again 10% to 12%, for the core business.

adds.what: New printing and binding facility (half complete in FY27, full completion FY28; partial operations Sept-Oct 2026)

growth.why: FY27 operating revenue growth guided at 10-15% (held), backed by NCERT adoption, West Bengal syllabus, content licensing target above Rs40 crore (Rs14 crore to date) and a new printing facility, though no hard order book or capacity numbers were quantified.
